plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: Wide, creamy-white blossoms with golden centers float on the still surface of ponds, lakes and slow rivers. Each flower rests on a raft of round, glossy green pads. The effect is serene, like a floating stage lit by sunshine.
plants.location: Ponds, lakes and slow waterways across Britain and temperate Europe
plants.funFact: The flowers open in the morning and close again in the afternoon. Their long stalks adjust as water levels change, so the blooms stay at the surface.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.description: Rugged, gnarled trees carry chunky, cylindrical flower spikes that look like bottle brushes. The spikes are packed with hundreds of tiny blooms. They glow pale green-cream and draw honeyeaters and other nectar-loving birds through the cooler months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to winter, peaking in autumn
plants.location: Coastal eastern Australia, from Queensland to Tasmania, where June falls in winter
plants.funFact: After flowering, the spikes become woody cones with seed pods that mostly stay shut. Heat from a bushfire makes the pods open and release their seeds, and this is how the species regenerates.
